mainTopic: The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram as a source for ביטול: the meaning of 'cooked', sixty versus one hundred, and the word 'זהו'
overview: The פסוק in במדבר 6:19 says the כהן takes the 'cooked foreleg' (זרוע בשלה) of the נזיר's ram. The foreleg goes only to a כהן, while the rest of the ram is eaten by the נזיר even if he is not a כהן. A ברייתא gives two readings of 'cooked': the תנא קמא says the foreleg is whole, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says it is cooked together with the ram. The גמרא offers two ways to explain their argument, and shows that under one of them everyone can learn the rule of ביטול from this case, while under the other only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי can. It then explains that the opinions of 'sixty' and 'one hundred' both come from the foreleg: one measures meat and bones, the other meat alone. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא that calls the foreleg 'זהו', 'this one', which seems to make it a one-time exception. אביי answers that 'זהו' is for רבי יהודה, who holds that a same-kind mixture is not nullified, based on the blood of the פר and שעיר. The foreleg is a חידוש that teaches no general rule, though it can still teach the stricter measures of sixty or one hundred. רבא answers instead that 'זהו' marks an exception to the rule of טעם כעיקר in קדשים.

steps.title: First opinion: 'cooked' means the foreleg is whole
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא of the ברייתא reads the word 'בשלה' in the פסוק as teaching that the foreleg must be whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'cooked' means nothing other than whole.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about the נזיר's ram. The first opinion (the תנא קמא) says the word 'בשלה' teaches that the foreleg is whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the כהן gets the 'cooked foreleg.' The תנא קמא learns from the word 'cooked' that the foreleg must be one whole piece, not cut into bits. He does not yet say whether it is cooked with the ram or apart from it, and the גמרא will look at that question soon.

keyTerms.meaning: The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram, which is given to the כהן (במדבר 6:19)
Cooked: the word in the פסוק being explained
'It is nothing other than': a way of saying what a word in the פסוק really means

phrases.english: "Cooked" means nothing other than whole.
phrases.notes: The word comes from במדבר 6:19, about the foreleg of the נזיר's ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about the cooked foreleg, which began before this part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, 'בשלה' teaches that the foreleg is whole.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: 'cooked' means cooked together with the ram
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי disagrees and reads 'בשלה' as teaching that the foreleg is cooked together with the ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: 'Cooked' means nothing other than that it was cooked with the ram.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא gives a different meaning to the word 'cooked.' רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says it means the foreleg was cooked together with the ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, the word 'cooked' is not about the foreleg being whole. It is about where it was cooked: in the same pot as the ram. This sets up the question the גמרא will now ask: what exactly are the two sides arguing about?

keyTerms.meaning: Ram: here, the נזיר's שלמים ram

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
"Cooked" means nothing other than that it was cooked with the ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different reading of the same word that the תנא קמא explained in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, 'בשלה' teaches that the foreleg is cooked together with the ram.

steps.title: First explanation: both cook it with the ram, but disagree on when to cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that everyone agrees the foreleg is cooked with the ram. The argument is only about whether it is cut off before cooking or after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that one cooks it with the ram. One Sage holds that one cuts it off and then cooks it, and the other Sage holds that one cooks it and then cuts it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what the two opinions in the ברייתא are really arguing about. In this first explanation, both agree the foreleg goes into the pot with the ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא, who said 'whole,' holds that you first cut off the whole foreleg and then cook it together with the ram. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי holds that you cook the whole ram first and only then cut off the foreleg. Either way, the foreleg and the rest of the ram are cooked together.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; both opinions accept this
One Sage holds... and the other Sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בשלה = שלימה' as meaning that the תנא קמא cooks the foreleg apart from the ram. In this explanation he also cooks it with the ram. He only cuts it off whole before cooking.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that one cooks it with the ram;

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ,
phrases.english: one Sage holds: one cuts it off and then cooks it,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who said the foreleg is 'whole': it is cut off whole, then cooked.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: one cooks it and then cuts it off.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the argument between the two opinions in steps 1 and 2 is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions agree the foreleg is cooked with the ram. They argue only about whether it is cut off before or after cooking.

steps.title: Second explanation: both cut it first, but disagree about which pot
steps.stepSummary: Another way to explain the argument: everyone agrees the foreleg is cut off first. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי cooks it with the ram, and the תנא קמא cooks it in a different pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: everyone agrees that one cuts it off and then cooks it. But one Sage holds that one cooks it with the ram, and the other Sage holds that one cooks it in another pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different explanation of the same argument. Now the question is whether the foreleg goes into the same pot as the ram or a separate pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the order is not in question, since both agree you cut first and cook after. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי cooks the foreleg together with the ram, while the תנא קמא cooks it in its own separate pot. So in this explanation, only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי has the foreleg cooked together with the rest of the ram.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead: brings in another possible explanation

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the order of the opinions flips here. In this step the first 'מר' is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי (with the ram), and the second is the תנא קמא (another pot).

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that one cuts it off and then cooks it;

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ מָר סָבַר: בַּהֲדֵי אַיִל מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ,
phrases.english: but one Sage holds: one cooks it with the ram,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, who said 'cooked with the ram.'

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: בִּקְדֵרָה אַחֶרֶת מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: one cooks it in another pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מְחַתֵּךְ לַהּ וַהֲדַר מְבַשֵּׁל לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the argument, different from the one in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions agree the foreleg is cut off first. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי cooks it with the ram, and the תנא קמא cooks it in a separate pot.

steps.title: Who can learn ביטול from the foreleg under each explanation
steps.stepSummary: Under the first explanation, everyone agrees the foreleg is cooked with the ram, so everyone can learn ביטול from it. Under the second explanation, only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי can.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the first version, it is according to everyone. According to the second version, it is only according to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what difference the two explanations make. It asks who can use the cooked foreleg as a source for the rule of ביטול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg goes only to a כהן, but the rest of the ram may be eaten by a non-כהן, even when the two were cooked together. That is the lesson about ביטול. In the first explanation everyone cooks them together, so everyone can learn it. In the second explanation the תנא קמא uses a separate pot, so only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי can learn it.

keyTerms.meaning: The view of everyone; all agree
Nullification: a forbidden taste or item does not make the rest forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram is a source for ביטול. Under the first explanation (both cook it with the ram), everyone accepts that source. Under the second explanation (the תנא קמא uses a separate pot), only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a small argument over cooking details decides whether a key source for ביטול is accepted by everyone or by only one opinion.

phrases.english: According to the first version, it is according to everyone;
phrases.notes: 'It' means learning ביטול from the foreleg cooked together with the ram.

phrases.aramaic: לְלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא – אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי.
phrases.english: according to the latter version, it is according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two explanations from steps 3 and 4 and shows how each one affects the source for ביטול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the first explanation, everyone can learn ביטול from the cooked foreleg. Under the second, only רבי שמעון בן יוחאי can.

steps.title: Where sixty and one hundred both come from
steps.stepSummary: Both numbers come from the foreleg of the נזיר's ram. The one who says 'sixty' compares meat and bones to meat and bones. The one who says 'one hundred' compares meat to meat only.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says ביטול happens in sixty holds that we compare the meat and bones of the foreleg to the meat and bones of the ram, and that gives sixty. The one who says one hundred holds that we compare meat to meat, and that gives one hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument about whether forbidden food is nullified in sixty or in one hundred. It shows that both opinions learn from the same foreleg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the foreleg is the source for ביטול. They only disagree about how to measure. If you count bones too, the foreleg is one part in sixty of the ram. If you count only meat, it is one part in one hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: We measure / we estimate the ratio
In sixty (nullified when there is sixty times more)

steps.whatToRemember: Sixty and one hundred are not two different sources. They are two ways of measuring the same foreleg: with bones (60) or without bones (100).

phrases.english: The one who says 'in sixty' holds:

phrases.aramaic: בָּשָׂר וַעֲצָמוֹת בַּהֲדֵי בָּשָׂר וַעֲצָמוֹת מְשַׁעֲרִינַן,
phrases.english: we measure meat and bones against meat and bones,
phrases.notes: He means the foreleg's meat and bones compared to the meat and bones of the rest of the ram.

phrases.english: and that comes out to sixty.
The one who says 'in one hundred' holds:
we measure meat against meat,
and that comes out to one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the foreleg as the source for ביטול and explains how each number is calculated from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sixty = measuring meat and bones together. One hundred = measuring meat alone. Both are measured from the foreleg compared to the ram.

steps.title: Can we really learn from the foreleg? The word 'זהו' seems to limit it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a ברייתא calls the foreleg case 'זהו היתר הבא מכלל איסור'. The word 'זהו' seems to say that only this case is nullified, and not other forbidden foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn from it? But a ברייתא teaches: 'This is a היתר that comes out of an איסור.' What does 'this is' come to exclude? Doesn't it exclude all other forbidden foods in the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the whole idea of learning ביטול from the foreleg. A ברייתא seems to say the foreleg is a one-time exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ram absorbs flavor from the foreleg, which is forbidden to the owner, yet the ram stays permitted. The ברייתא says 'זהו', meaning 'this one'. That sounds like it shuts out every other איסור, so no general rule of ביטול could be learned from here.

keyTerms.meaning: But do we really learn from it?
Something permitted that comes out of a forbidden category

steps.confusionAlert: The קשיא is not saying the foreleg is not nullified. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only whether this case can serve as a model for all other איסורים.

phrases.english: And do we learn from it?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
This is a permitted thing that comes out of a forbidden category,
phrases.notes: The ram tasted of the forbidden foreleg, yet it is still permitted.

phrases.english: What does 'this is' come to exclude?
Doesn't it come to exclude all the forbidden foods in the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic idea behind steps 5 and 6, that ביטול is learned from the foreleg.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that general ביטול rules are learned from the foreleg of the נזיר's ram.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'זהו' in the ברייתא sounds like it limits ביטול to this one case and excludes all other איסורים.

steps.title: אביי: 'זהו' is needed for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'זהו' is written for רבי יהודה, who holds that a mixture of the same kind is not nullified. The ברייתא teaches that here, in this case, it is nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is needed only for רבי יהודה, who says a mixture of the same kind is not nullified. It teaches us that here it is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing what 'זהו' is excluding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg and the ram are the same kind of meat. רבי יהודה normally holds מין במינו לא בטל. So 'זהו' does not exclude all other איסורים from ביטול. It says that only here does a same-kind mixture get nullified, according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of the same kind

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: אביי said: It is needed only according to רבי יהודה,
who says that a kind mixed with its own kind is not nullified,
so it teaches us that here it is nullified.
phrases.notes: Foreleg meat and ram meat are the same kind, so this is a same-kind mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by reading 'זהו' differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the exclusion to one opinion (רבי יהודה) and one type of mixture (מין במינו).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זהו' excludes every other איסור in the Torah from ביטול.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זהו' only excludes other same-kind mixtures, according to רבי יהודה. For everyone else, the foreleg can still teach a general ביטול rule.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה learn a general rule from the foreleg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the foreleg shows that a same-kind mixture is nullified, why doesn't רבי יהודה learn from it that all same-kind mixtures are nullified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's answer. If the foreleg is nullified though it is the same kind, רבי יהודה should apply that to every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a case in the Torah becomes a model for other cases. So why should רבי יהודה treat the foreleg as a one-time exception instead of a general rule against his own view?

phrases.english: And let him learn from it?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יהודה. Let him learn that every same-kind mixture is nullified.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that מין במינו לא בטל, in light of the foreleg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The foreleg is a same-kind mixture that is nullified, so it should teach a general rule that same-kind mixtures are nullified.

steps.title: The blood of the פר and שעיר shows same-kind is not nullified
steps.stepSummary: The Torah shows the opposite with the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור. The two bloods are mixed together, yet the Torah still calls it 'the blood of the שעיר', so it was not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah revealed: 'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat.' The two are mixed together, and they are not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה cannot learn a general rule from the foreleg. Another פסוק shows that a same-kind mixture is not nullified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull has much more blood than the goat. Still, the Torah calls the mixture 'the blood of the goat' too, so the goat's blood keeps its identity. That is רבי יהודה's source for מין במינו לא בטל. The foreleg stays a special exception, which is why 'זהו' is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of the bull and the blood of the goat (יום כיפור)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה there are two sources. The blood of the פר and שעיר is the general rule: same-kind is not nullified. The foreleg is the exception, marked by 'זהו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why one case in the Torah does not automatically become a general rule. When another פסוק teaches the opposite, the first case is treated as an exception.

phrases.english: The Merciful One revealed:
"And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat,"
both of them are mixed together with each other,
and they are not nullified.
phrases.notes: The bull has more blood, yet the goat's blood still counts by name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by bringing a פסוק that teaches the opposite rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a competing פסוק that sets the general rule, so the foreleg remains an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה should learn from the foreleg that every same-kind mixture is nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood of the פר and שעיר teaches that same-kind mixtures are not nullified. The foreleg is a special exception, so 'זהו' is needed for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why learn from the blood and not from the foreleg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה learns from the blood of the פר and שעיר (not nullified) instead of from the foreleg (nullified).
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did you choose to learn from the blood case? Learn instead from the foreleg case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10. There are two Torah cases that point in opposite directions, so why does רבי יהודה follow the blood case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg shows that a same-kind mixture is nullified. The blood of the פר and שעיר shows that a same-kind mixture is not nullified. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing the blood case as the model.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this option over the other one?
We learn, we derive a rule from a source

phrases.english: And what did you see that we learn from that one,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the blood of the פר and שעיר from step 10.

phrases.english: let him learn from this one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source chosen in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the blood of the פר and שעיר as רבי יהודה's model
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two Torah sources point in opposite directions, and nothing has been said yet to prefer one over the other.

steps.title: The foreleg is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The foreleg is a חידוש, an unusual rule, and we do not build general rules from a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a novelty, and we do not learn from a novelty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the foreleg case is a one-time special rule, so it cannot teach about other mixtures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חידוש breaks the normal pattern, so it stays limited to its own case. That is why רבי יהודה builds his general rule on the blood case instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A novelty, a special rule that goes against the normal pattern
We do not learn general rules from a special case

steps.whatToRemember: A חידוש stays in its own case. We do not stretch it to other cases.

phrases.english: It is a novelty,
phrases.notes: Normally you may not mix in something forbidden on purpose to nullify it, yet here the Torah has you cook the foreleg with the ram.

phrases.english: and we do not learn from a novelty.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a source: the foreleg is a חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources are equal, so either one could be the model.
steps.terutzMaskana: The foreleg is a חידוש and cannot be a model. The blood case is the general rule.

steps.title: Then don't learn sixty or one hundred from it either
steps.stepSummary: If the foreleg is a חידוש, the numbers sixty and one hundred should not be learned from it either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also not learn the measure of one hundred or sixty from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 12. If we do not learn from a חידוש, how can the numbers sixty and one hundred come from the foreleg?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, both measures for nullifying a mixture of different kinds came from the foreleg. If the foreleg cannot teach anything outside its own case, those numbers seem to lose their source.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if what you said is true
One hundred or sixty: the two measures for nullifying forbidden food

phrases.english: If so,
let him also not learn for one hundred or sixty?
phrases.notes: These are the 'one hundred' and 'sixty' opinions from step 6. Both come from the foreleg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְמֵאָה וְשִׁשִּׁים נָמֵי לָא לִיגְמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the rule from step 12 against the numbers in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the sixty or one hundred measure from the foreleg
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חידוש teaches nothing beyond its own case, the measures learned from it should also fall away.

steps.title: The numbers are learned only as a stringency
steps.stepSummary: The measures of sixty and one hundred are learned to be stricter, because by Torah law a simple majority would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we learn a leniency from it? We learn a stringency, because by Torah law forbidden food is nullified in a simple majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that learning sixty or one hundred from the foreleg is not using the חידוש to be lenient. It is used to be stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the foreleg, the Torah law would be that forbidden food is nullified in a simple majority, which is easy. Sixty or one hundred is much harder to reach, so this is a stringency. Using a חידוש to add strictness is not the problem that 'we do not learn from a חידוש' was worried about.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Do you really think?
It is nullified in a majority

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sixty or one hundred rule makes things easier. Compared to the basic Torah rule of רוב, it makes things harder.

phrases.english: Is that to say we learn it for a leniency?
We learn it for a stringency,
since by Torah law it is nullified in a majority.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the derivation as a stringency, not a leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning the numbers from the foreleg uses a חידוש to be lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: Compared to the Torah rule of רוב, the numbers are stricter, so learning them is allowed.

steps.title: רבא: 'זהו' is about flavor counting like substance
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to step 7. The word 'זהו' teaches that in the foreleg case the ram is permitted, even though with קדשים the flavor of food usually forbids like the food itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The word was needed only for the rule that flavor is like substance. With sacred foods that makes things forbidden. The ברייתא teaches us that here it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question about 'זהו' from step 7 in a new way, different from אביי's answer in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, if the flavor of sacred food spreads into other food, that food becomes forbidden (טעם כעיקר). The ברייתא's 'זהו' says this case is different: the rest of the ram stays permitted. So 'זהו' is not limiting ביטול in general. It marks an exception to the strict טעם כעיקר rule of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Flavor counts like the substance itself

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for 'זהו': אביי says it is for רבי יהודה (step 8), and רבא says it marks an exception to טעם כעיקר in קדשים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It was needed only for 'flavor is like substance,'
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word זהו in the ברייתא from step 7.

phrases.english: which with sacred foods is forbidden,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word 'זהו' as marking an exception to טעם כעיקר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זהו' means only the foreleg is nullified, and no other forbidden food.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זהו' teaches that in this case of קדשים the flavor does not forbid, so the ram is permitted.
